title: HTTPS & encryption
hook: HTTPS is the same request/response — wrapped so a snoop on the wire can’t read it.

steps.caption: Your browser and the server set up an encrypted session (TLS).

nodeCaptions.client: Certificates help you know you’re talking to the real server.
nodeCaptions.server: After handshake, application data is encrypted.

steps.caption: The HTTP request travels encrypted. A snoop sees ciphertext, not your password.

nodeCaptions.snoop: Can still see that you’re talking to an IP — not the contents.
nodeCaptions.server: Decrypts with the session keys and handles normal HTTP.

takeaways: HTTPS = HTTP plus TLS encryption and authentication of the server.
Encryption hides contents from on-path observers, not from the server itself.
Metadata (that you connected) can still leak.

quiz.question: What does HTTPS protect from a network snoop?
choices: The fact that you connected to a server
The readable contents of your request and response
A stolen laptop unlocked on your desk
quiz.explanation: TLS encrypts the payload. Endpoint compromise is a different problem.
